record.original_question: Let phi(k, G) denote the number of k-matchings in G, and let lambda(k, n, r) be the minimum of phi(k, G) over all r-regular bipartite multigraphs G on 2n vertices. Is it always true that for every 1 <= k <= n, lambda(k, n, r) is at least ((n choose k)^2) * ((nr - k) / nr)^(rn-k) * ((kr) / n)^k?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a multigraph $G$, let $\phi(k,G)$ denote the number of $k$-matchings in $G$ (i.e., the number of sets of $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint edges). Let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{bi,mult}}(2n,r)$ denote the class of $r$-regular bipartite multigraphs on $2n$ vertices (with both color classes of size $n$). Define
$$\lambda(k,n,r) := \min\{\phi(k,G) : G \in \mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{bi,mult}}(2n,r)\}.$$
Prove or disprove: for all integers $n \ge 1$, $r \ge 1$, and $1 \le k \le n$,
$$\lambda(k,n,r) \;\ge\; \binom{n}{k}^{2}\left(\frac{nr-k}{nr}\right)^{nr-k}\left(\frac{kr}{n}\right)^{k}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Lower Matching Conjecture was proved by P. Csikvári (arXiv:1406.0766, published in J. Eur. Math. Soc.), where he establishes the conjectured lower bound for the number of k-matchings in r-regular bipartite (multi)graphs and also gives new proofs of Schrijver's and Gurvits's theorems. An asymptotic version had earlier been proved by Gurvits.
